title: We just hit 6,000 MCP servers — and the ecosystem will never look small again
excerpt: Influzer.ai’s MCP directory just crossed 6,000 listings. From 1,500 in June to six thousand now. This is not a vanity scrape — it is the moment the catalog became infrastructure.
contentHtml:
We just hit 6,000 MCP servers.

Say it again: six thousand Model Context Protocol servers in the Influzer.ai registry. In June we celebrated 1,500 listings. A few days ago we were almost there. Today the live catalog sits above six thousand — with thousands of indexed tools across 12 categories.

That number is not a scrape scoreboard. It is what happens when weekly registry syncs, daily tools/list validation, community submissions, and a tools-first Top 100 all keep compounding.

Why this milestone is huge:

  • The long tail is now the product — niche databases, browsers, SaaS connectors, memory servers, and hosted endpoints are searchable in one place
  • “Search the registry first” beats “build another wrapper” more often than it did six months ago
  • Agents care about indexed tools, not GitHub stars — and the directory is built around that signal

Six thousand is a checkpoint, not a finish line. Servers still churn. Listings still need honest tool data. Builders still need a path to get found.

Celebrate with us: browse the full directory, start from the Top 100, connect Influzer MCP Discovery inside Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor — or submit a server we are still missing.

If you ship MCP, the ecosystem is no longer a spreadsheet problem. It is a discovery problem — and that is exactly what Influzer is for.
